subject: POC trial planning & workload intake - AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: POC next steps & workload intake

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC: 

Summary of what you asked for:
- 2-week POC to validate latency, throughput, and cost for your primary triage/summary pipeline
- Success criteria: 95th percentile tail latency < 300ms for single-request path, average token cost below $0.0006/token, and qualitative parity on summaries (sample prompts) vs current baseline 
- Evaluation plan: run 10k representative requests across peak/burst windows, compare latency and cost, and run a blind quality eval on 150 sample inputs

Workload/traffic we captured on the call (please confirm):
- Baseline RPS: 12 RPS sustained
- Peak RPS: 120 RPS for brief bursts (1-2 min) during scheduled batch processing
- Typical prompt token lengths: 60-250 tokens (median ~110)
- Expected concurrency from app: 40 concurrent connections during peak
- Burst pattern: daily morning spike 08:00-09:00 PST and an ad-hoc 5-10 minute spike when batch jobs run

Proposed owner & next actions:
1) Redwood: Ben to schedule an architecture/ops sync with your infra and SRE (Dylan to join) - propose Wed 6/30 10:00am PT
2) AcmeHealth: Sara to provide a sample workload CSV or load_profile.xlsx (RPS timeline + payload size distribution) + SOC2 snapshot if available
3) Redwood SE: Marissa to prepare a POC playbook (config, metrics, eval script) and a preset quantization recommendation for cost testing

Deliverables by kickoff:
- Workload profile (CSV/XLSX) from AcmeHealth
- POC plan + evaluation checklist from Redwood
- Scheduled kickoff meeting

If anything above is off, let me know and I’ll adjust. Otherwise I’ll send a calendar invite for the architecture sync.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap - that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 120 RPS peak is correct but typically lasts 60-90 seconds; we can provide a sample 24-hr RPS time series.
- Median tokens are closer to 95 for triage prompts; the 250 token tail is for the long context follow-ups.
- Concurrency: our proxy multiplexes to 30 connections normally; we can hit 50 during load tests.

We’ll attach the workload spreadsheet (load_profile.xlsx) and a redacted SOC2 snapshot for your security review. John will start the internal procurement paperwork next week - deal id ACME-2345.

I’m available Wed 6/30 10:00am PT for the architecture sync.

Sara Lowe
Director, ML Platforms | AcmeHealth
sara.lowe@acmehealth.com

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:45:00 -0700

Perfect - thanks Sara. I’ve got Wed 6/30 10:00am PT on my calendar and will send the invite with a short agenda.

Marissa / Dylan - FYI on the workload details. A couple quick asks before the call so we can prepare the environment:
- Can you confirm whether we want to exercise continuous batching vs low-latency single-request path for the initial run? My recommendation: run both but prioritize the single-request SLO for the first set of 5k requests.
- Marissa: can you draft the evaluation checklist (metrics to capture + sample prompts) and attach any seeding scripts we’ll use to compare quality?

Sara - once we have the load_profile.xlsx we’ll convert it to an internal traffic replay (RPS timeline + token distributions) and share the POC playbook.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: POC next steps & workload intake

Thanks Ben - quick technical questions / notes ahead of tomorrow: 

1) Workload conversion: please include a column for "input token length" and "expected output token length" (we’ll simulate both). If possible include timestamps in epoch ms so we can recreate burst patterns.
2) Concurrency model: confirm whether your client pools requests behind a single load balancer (so we test at the edge) or you can generate concurrent connections from multiple IPs - latter helps validate connection scaling.
3) Failure modes: do you expect timeouts to be retried by the app? If yes, include retry semantics (backoff, max attempts).

Proposed evaluation checklist (high level):
- Latency: P50 / P95 / P99 per request path and per token
- Cost: tokenized cost per request and aggregate cost for test load
- Quality: blind eval on 150 samples using your baseline rubric (precision/recall markers + qualitative notes)
- Reliability: successful requests % during spikes and during rolling restart

I’ll prepare a draft playbook and a script to convert load_profile.xlsx to our replay format; will attach that into the invite.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: poc_playbook_draft.md (stub)
From: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: John Peterson <john.peterson@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: POC next steps & workload intake

Marissa - thanks for the checklist - that looks good. A few answers inline:
- We included input and output token length columns and epoch timestamps in the load_profile.xlsx.
- Concurrency: our test harness can generate traffic from 3 separate worker VMs to approximate multiple client IPs; we will provide the script and the VM setup notes.
- Retries: app does up to 2 retries with exponential backoff (200ms -> 800ms). We will document that.

Timeline confirmation:
- Kickoff + architecture sync: Wed 6/30 10:00am PT
- Workload ingestion & baseline run: week of 7/5 (target Wed 7/7)
- Quality evaluation & report: week of 7/12
- POC wrap + decision meeting: 7/21

Success criteria reminder (from leadership):
- Performance: P95 < 300ms on single-request path during baseline traffic; P99 < 800ms during simulated bursts
- Cost: token cost at or below our target (we provided target $0.0006/token)
- Quality: automated eval score within 5% of current baseline on provided rubric

I’ve attached the files to this thread. Looking forward to tomorrow.

Sara
